BiblicalUsage: Chadar is a name that lives in a spelling. The King James prints Hadar in the list of Ishmael's sons in Genesis, but the Hebrew text behind it reads Hadad, the same name given in Chronicles. Strong's keeps Chadar as its own entry because some copies read it with an r, and the word itself never stands anywhere else in the Hebrew Bible.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God lets the variant stand without letting it confuse the story — one son of Ishmael, whether the copy says Hadar or Hadad.
